newsitem.title: USA: Ex-CBOE chairman joins ABN AMRO unit.
newsitem.headline: Ex-CBOE chairman joins ABN AMRO unit.

text.p: Alger "Duke" Chapman, who last month retired as chairman of the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), will join ABN AMRO Chicago Corp (AACC) as vice chairman, the firm said on Thursday.

Chapman will be based in Chicago, with responsibility for building personal financial services business at sister subsidiaries of ABN AMRO North America Inc, which itself is an arm of the Dutch parent, ABN AMRO Holding NV, AACC said.
AACC, capitalized at $450 million, is the product of a merger in January between ABN AMRO Securities (USA) Inc and Chicago Corp.

"His unparalled accomplishments in defining and delivering personal financial services make him a tremendous asset to our organization," Jack Wing, chairman and chief executive officer of AACC, said in a statement.
Chapman, prior to his tenure at CBOE, was vice chairman of American Express Bank Ltd in the early 1980s, where he was in charge of building high net-worth private banking business.
The ABN AMRO subsidiaries Chapman would be involved with included LaSalle National Bank, LaSalle Bank FSB, LaSalle Bank NI, LaSalle Bank N.A. and LaSalle Bank, AACC said.
